title: Measles Cases in the U.S. Are at a 35-Year High
snippet:
Editor at Large

Measles is an old scourge that’s rapidly re-emerging as a new one. According to numbers released by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) on July 24, there have been 2,318 cases of measles reported nationwide so far in this year, already exceeding the 2,289 cases reported in all of 2025. The current figure is the highest incidence of measles in 35 years, a record set back in 1991 when there were 9,643 U.S. cases. [...] That much of a drop in vaccination coverage creates pockets for viruses, like the one that causes measles, to spread. Of measles cases so far in 2026 and for the entirety of last year, 93% have been among unvaccinated children, 3% were among children who received just one vaccine dose, and 4% were among kids who received both. This year, 7% of those cases resulted in hospitalizations. There have been no deaths so far this year, but there were three in 2025—one of them an unvaccinated adult, and [...] It wasn’t long ago that measles cases were extremely rare in the U.S. In 1963, the first measles vaccine was introduced in the U.S., and decades of steady administration of the shot eventually led to the country being declared measles-free in 2000. There were some scattered infections in the ensuing years—56 cases in 2003, 55 in 2012, 13 in 2020. But this year and last year, the numbers have exploded.

title: History of Measles
snippet:
In 1954, John F. Enders and Dr. Thomas C. Peebles collected blood samples from several ill students during a measles outbreak in Boston, Massachusetts. They wanted to isolate the measles virus in the student's blood and create a measles vaccine. They succeeded in isolating measles in 13-year-old David Edmonston's blood. [...] measles virus

## Pre-vaccine era

Francis Home, a Scottish physician, demonstrated in 1757 that measles is caused by an infectious agent in the blood of patients.

In 1912, measles became a nationally notifiable disease in the United States, requiring U.S. healthcare providers and laboratories to report all diagnosed cases. In the first decade of reporting, an average of 6,000 measles-related deaths were reported each year. [...] In 1963, John Enders and colleagues transformed their Edmonston-B strain of measles virus into a vaccine and licensed it in the United States. In 1968, an improved and even weaker measles vaccine, developed by Maurice Hilleman and colleagues, began to be distributed. This vaccine, called the Edmonston-Enders (formerly "Moraten") strain has been the only measles vaccine used in the United States since 1968.

title: US measles cases hit 2,318 in 2026, surpassing last year's total: CDC - ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
snippet: # US measles cases hit 2,318 in 2026, surpassing last year's total: CDC. This marks the highest number of cases recorded since 1991. The number of confirmed measles cases in the U.S. so far this year has hit 2,318, surpassing the total reported for all last year, according to data updated Friday from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Previously, last year's total of 2,289 was the highest number of recorded measles cases in more than 30 years, CDC data shows. Sixteen of this year's total have been among international visitors to the U.S., according to the CDC. The majority of measles cases in 2026 have been confirmed among children and teenagers aged 19 and younger, according to the CDC. Meanwhile, 3% of cases are among those who have received just one dose of the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine and 4% of cases are among those who received the recommended two doses, according to the CDC.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has warned of rising measles transmission in parts of the country in their latest case data. Laboratory reports show 106 additional confirmed infections since the previous update, bringing England’s total for the year to 736 cases between 1 January and 8 June - against 959 confirmed cases during all of 2025.
